front: Effects of ionising radiation on living things?
How do you choose an isotope for a use?
back: By its type of radiation (penetration, ionisation) and its half-life (how long it must last).

front: How does a smoke alarm work?
back: Alpha particles ionise air so a current flows; smoke absorbs them, the current drops and the alarm sounds.
Gamma rays penetrate packaging and kill microbes; the items do not become radioactive.
Beta source with a long half-life; thicker paper absorbs more, lowering the count rate.
Gamma emitters with short half-lives (hours), e.g. technetium-99m.
Tongs, never point at people, lead-lined locked storage, short use, dosimeters for workers.
Less time, more distance, more shielding.
